questions.question: Describe the concept of training in crop plants. Discuss its objectives and various methods with suitable examples.
questions.solution_html:
• methods with suitable examples.
  • Definition: Training is the practice of directing and controlling the growth of a young fruit
  • plant into a desired shape or framework by tying, supporting, bending, or selectively removing
  • shoots. ((2 marks))
  • Objectives of Training: (Any 2 points - (2 marks))
  • - Develop a strong framework capable of bearing heavy fruit loads.
  • - Maintain proper tree shape and size.
  • - Improve light penetration and air circulation.
  • - Facilitate orchard operations (pruning, spraying, harvesting, intercultural operations).
  • - Increase photosynthetic efficiency and reduce wind/load breakage.
  • - Improve fruit colour, size, quality, and pest management.
  • Methods of Training: (Any 4 methods with examples - (6 marks))
  • Open Centre System (Vase System): Central leader removed after planting; 3-5 scaffold branches
  • grow outward forming an open centre for better sunlight. Eg: Apple, peach, mango, guava.
  • Central Leader System: Main trunk grows uninterrupted; lateral branches arise regularly, forming a
  • pyramidal shape with strong structural support. Eg: Pear, walnut, sapota.
  • Cordon System: Single strong shoot grown to desired height, then bent and tied horizontally along
  • supporting wires to form permanent arms maintained by annual pruning. Eg: Grapes, passion
  • fruit, vanilla.
  • Head System (Bush System): Main trunk kept short (30-90 cm). 4-6 primary branches arise from
  • the head giving a bush-like appearance. Eg: Grapes, pepper.
  • Bower (Pergola) System: Vines grow over an overhead network of wires supported by pillars to
  • form a roof-like canopy. Eg: Grapes, passion fruit, bitter gourd.
  • [10 x 1 = (10 Marks)]

questions.question: Describe the concept of training in crop plants. Discuss its objectives and various methods with suitable examples.
questions.solution_html:
• methods with suitable examples.
  • Definition: Training is the practice of directing and controlling the growth of a young fruit
  • plant into a desired shape or framework by tying, supporting, bending, or selectively removing
  • shoots. ((2 marks))
  • Objectives of Training: (Any 2 points - (2 marks))
  • - Develop a strong framework capable of bearing heavy fruit loads.
  • - Maintain proper tree shape and size.
  • - Improve light penetration and air circulation.
  • - Facilitate orchard operations (pruning, spraying, harvesting, intercultural operations).
  • - Increase photosynthetic efficiency and reduce wind/load breakage.
  • - Improve fruit colour, size, quality, and pest management.
  • Methods of Training: (Any 4 methods with examples - (6 marks))
  • Open Centre System (Vase System): Central leader removed after planting; 3-5 scaffold branches
  • grow outward forming an open centre for better sunlight. Eg: Apple, peach, mango, guava.
  • Central Leader System: Main trunk grows uninterrupted; lateral branches arise regularly, forming a
  • pyramidal shape with strong structural support. Eg: Pear, walnut, sapota.
  • Cordon System: Single strong shoot grown to desired height, then bent and tied horizontally along
  • supporting wires to form permanent arms maintained by annual pruning. Eg: Grapes, passion
  • fruit, vanilla.
  • Head System (Bush System): Main trunk kept short (30-90 cm). 4-6 primary branches arise from
  • the head giving a bush-like appearance. Eg: Grapes, pepper.
  • Bower (Pergola) System: Vines grow over an overhead network of wires supported by pillars to
  • form a roof-like canopy. Eg: Grapes, passion fruit, bitter gourd.
  • [10 x 1 = (10 Marks)]
